title: Enhancement: GCU: Need a better way to evaluate generated plans
author: bhouse-nexthop
body:
### Is it platform specific

generic

### Importance or Severity

Medium

### Description of the enhancement

GCU right now is a black box, you input your new config or a patch to apply, and it outputs a patch set based on generators and validators.  GCU may try thousands or tens of thousands of paths before it finds one that works. Sometimes these outputs can be wildly bad (suboptimal).

Having visibility into the order the generators are run, and why certain paths weren't taken would greatly improve the ability to debug suboptimal paths that are generated.  These suboptimal paths may be bugs or simply some new edge case that a new generator is needed for.

Right now you basically have to take guesses at what may have caused an issue and just try various tweaks to solve it.  Having the ability to see what is happening behind the scenes will make correcting such issues much easier in the future.

### Current Behavior

No ability to trace GCU.

### Proposed Behavior

Ability to trace GCU.

linkedPullRequests.title: GCU: Add path tracing support
linkedPullRequests.author: bhouse-nexthop
linkedPullRequests.body:
#### What I did

GCU uses a very complex set of generators and validators.  When a suboptimal plan is created, it can be hard to determine why the path was generated the way it was and how best to optimize the generators.

This patch adds the ability to pass an IO object to all attempted paths with annotations such as `valid`, `invalid`, `recurse_reject` (source and target were already attempted), and `path_issue` (patch was good, but a generator further down the hierarchy failed).  It will also list the generator used for each patch, and if `invalid` it will list the validator which failed it with a possibly extended error message.

For callers to `config replace` or `config apply-patch` a new command line option of `--path-trace` which takes a filename to dump the json output.

This patch also increases the diff output shown during test run failures to make it easier to debug issues based on logging generated via CI/CD.

Fixes https://github.com/sonic-net/sonic-buildimage/issues/25748

#### How I did it

Modified various classes and functions to pass around objects and metadata needed to generate the trace.

#### How to verify it

Run `config replace` or `config apply-patch` with the `--path-trace` argument.
